title: Hybrid retrieval with a real pretrained dense model, on real documents
goal: Re-measure EXP-004-style hybrid retrieval with a real pretrained encoder for the dense leg, over the real document collection from EXP-025 instead of synthetic lease passages.
method: Both indexes share the same Okapi BM25 sparse leg (lab/common/index.BM25, unchanged). The classical index's dense leg is sklearn TfidfVectorizer cosine (EXP-004's substitute). The real index's dense leg is mean-pooled spaCy en_core_web_md static word vectors, min-max normalized and averaged 0.5/0.5 with the sparse score, same fusion formula as lab/common/index.Index. Two query sets run over the same 76 real passages from 25 real documents: (1) each chunk's own verified-substring extractive summary, gold is that chunk's id -- a sanity check where the query is literally inside the gold passage; (2) each document's real headline, gold is every chunk of that document's body -- a harder test where the query wording is not copied into any chunk.

summary_queries_sanity_check.note: query is a literal substring of the gold passage; both scorers can win on exact overlap

headline_queries_hard_test.note: query is the article's real headline, not copied verbatim into any chunk body

real_model_card.ner_training_data: OntoNotes 5 (real pretrained checkpoint, shipped by spaCy)
real_model_card.vector_training_data: GloVe-style static vectors trained on a large web/news crawl, shipped by spaCy
real_model_card.huggingface_block_detail: huggingface.co CONNECT rejected with 403 by this sandbox's egress policy

results_prose: Sanity check (75 substring-summary queries, 76 passages): classical Recall@5 1.0, real-model Recall@5 1.0 (lift +0.0000) -- both near ceiling because the query is literally inside the gold passage. Hard test (25 real-headline queries, gold is the whole document's chunk set): classical Recall@5 0.7379, Recall@10 0.869; real-model Recall@5 0.6769, Recall@10 0.7741 (lift -0.0610 at 5, -0.0949 at 10). On this harder, more realistic test the real pretrained static-vector dense leg does not beat classical TF-IDF; it measures lower. The measured number is reported as found, not adjusted.
conclusion: The real pretrained dense leg is measured against the classical TF-IDF dense leg on the same real corpus and the same two query sets. See real_model_card in the metrics for exactly which checkpoint ran and why it is not bge-small-en-v1.5. The two tests disagree: on the substring sanity check both legs sit at the Recall@5/10 ceiling, matching EXP-004's own 'reranker lift 0.0' finding on an easy set. On the harder headline test the real pretrained static-vector leg scores lower than classical TF-IDF (Recall@5 and @10 both negative lift). A plausible reason: mean-pooling 300-d vectors over a short, all-caps wire headline likely washes out the few content words that matter, while TF-IDF's rare-term weighting keeps exact shared tokens (a name, a commodity) salient. This closes the EXP-029 rerun todo for the embeddings component -- it is no longer unrun -- but the honest result is that this particular real pretrained encoder did not outperform the classical substitute on real documents at this scale.
scale_down: 25 real documents / 76 chunks, not a 1,000-page collection (EXP-022 on-disk index is still a separate todo). bge-small-en-v1.5, Qdrant sparse vectors, and bge-reranker-v2-m3 remain unloaded because huggingface.co is blocked by this sandbox's egress policy; see real_model_card.

models_used: Real pretrained spaCy en_core_web_md static word vectors (GloVe-style, trained on a web/news crawl) for the dense leg, fused with the unchanged in-process Okapi BM25 sparse leg. bge-small-en-v1.5, Qdrant, and bge-reranker-v2-m3 were not loaded: huggingface.co is blocked in this sandbox (403 CONNECT, policy denial). This is a real, reachable, non-generative encoder, not the exact blueprint checkpoint. See lab/common/real_models.py:model_card().
